title: Maximize Distance to Closest Person
statement:
The array `seats` describes one row of seats from left to right: `seats[i]` is `1` when seat `i` is already taken and `0` when it is free. You are going to sit in one of the free seats. The distance between seats `i` and `j` is `|i - j|`, and what matters to you is the distance to the nearest taken seat.

Pick the free seat that makes that nearest distance as large as possible and return the distance. The row always has at least one free seat and at least one taken seat.
notes:
## Intuition

The brute force tries every free seat and scans the row for the nearest taken one, which is O(n²). It is enough to look at the empty stretches between taken seats instead. A stretch at the very start or end of the row has a person on one side only, so sitting at the wall gives a distance equal to the whole stretch. A stretch between two taken seats at `prev` and `i` is best used from its middle, giving `floor((i - prev) / 2)`. Two indices moving left to right, `prev` trailing `i`, find every stretch in one pass.

## Approach

1. Set `prev = -1` (no taken seat seen yet) and `best = 0`.
2. Move `i` across the row and skip free seats.
3. At the first taken seat, the stretch before it touches the left wall, so `best = i`.
4. At any later taken seat, the stretch from `prev` to `i` gives `floor((i - prev) / 2)`; keep the larger of that and `best`.
5. Move `prev` to `i`.
6. After the loop, the stretch after `prev` touches the right wall and gives `n - 1 - prev`; return the larger of that and `best`.

## Example 1, step by step

`seats = [1, 0, 0, 0, 1, 0, 1]`, `n = 7`.

- `i = 0` is taken and `prev = -1`, so `best = 0` (no seats on the left), then `prev = 0`.
- `i = 4` is taken: the gap gives `floor((4 - 0) / 2) = 2`, so `best = 2`, `prev = 4`.
- `i = 6` is taken: `floor((6 - 4) / 2) = 1`, `best` stays 2, `prev = 6`.
- The right edge gives `7 - 1 - 6 = 0`. The answer is `2` (sit at seat 2).

## Complexity

- Time: O(n): each seat is visited once.
- Space: O(1): only a few indices are kept.

## Pitfalls

- An edge stretch is not halved: with `[0, 0, 0, 1]` you sit at seat 0 and get 3, not 1.
- Halve an inner gap with integer division; `(i - prev) / 2` alone gives 1.5 for a gap of 3.
- Do not forget the stretch after the last taken seat, which the loop never closes.

## Variables

| Name | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `n` | number of seats |
| `prev` | index of the last taken seat seen, or -1 before the first |
| `i` | index of the seat being looked at |
| `best` | the largest nearest-person distance found so far |

narration.3: No taken seat has been seen yet, so prev starts before the row.
narration.4: best holds the largest distance found so far.
narration.6: Walk i across the row; prev trails behind at the last taken seat.
narration.7: Free seats do not end a stretch, so skip them.
narration.10: Is this the first taken seat in the row?
narration.11: Then the seats before it touch the wall: sitting at seat 0 gives distance i.
narration.13: Otherwise sit in the middle of the gap between prev and i, which gives half the gap rounded down.
narration.15: This taken seat becomes the left end of the next gap.
narration.17: The seats after the last taken one touch the right wall; compare that stretch too and return the best.
